transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-30
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Ari (Quantaco Head of ML), Priya (Quantaco Infra), Marco (Quantaco Product)

Summary (auto): quick cost review, agreed next benchmarks, share pricing and enable cache TTL test.

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do the usual 45 minutes. main goal is to go over the cost numbers from last week's runs and decide what tuning to try next.
00:12 - Ari: Yep thanks, excited. we saw some promising numbers but want to understand tokens per dollar and whether caching is giving us solid savings or just warm start bias.
00:25 - Jonah: quick context last run was 12 hours on the hosted test cluster, model was r-7b-quant (8-bit quant), batching set to 64 max, dynamic scheduler, prefix cache enabled for 30m TTL.
00:40 - Priya: and infra note, that run used shared hosted capacity not dedicated, so noisy neighbors might bias throughput numbers down a bit.
00:52 - Jonah: right, we tried to correct for that by running three windows and taking median. raw tokens generated ~18.2M tokens over 12h, average tokens/sec ~42, effective tokens/sec/$ (hosted pricing) we calculated to ~1,150 tokens per USD for that config.
01:12 - Marco: wait that tokens per dollar number, how did you compute it? is that including request overheads like preproc and embeddings?
01:19 - Jonah: good point. the baseline includes generation tokens only; we left out embedding calls in the model run (we ran separate embedding test). total end-to-end tokens/sec/$ will be lower when you include embedding and downstream postprocessing.
01:35 - Ari: what's the p95 latency on that config? we need p95 under 600ms for our customer use case.
01:42 - Jonah: p95 about 520ms on median windows, p50 ~210ms. when we cranked batching higher (max 128) throughput increased to ~62 tokens/sec but p95 jumped to ~920ms. so tradeoff there.
01:59 - Maya: so smaller batches keep latency tight but reduce tokens/sec/$, larger batches up throughput but risk missing p95 SLO. we should quantify how much cost we save per 100ms increase in p95.
02:15 - Priya: also curious about cache savings. can you remind us what cache hit rate looked like?
02:20 - Jonah: on sample production workload the prefix/KV cache hit was ~27% overall. that translated to about 24% fewer generated tokens and roughly 18% reduction in billed token cost in hosted pricing for that test window. caveat cache hits skew towards certain user journeys that are repetitive.
02:40 - Marco: so in practical terms, with cache enabled we're looking at maybe 15-25% cost savings depending on traffic mix.
02:48 - Ari: is that consistent across dayparts? like bursts vs stable traffic?
02:52 - Jonah: bursts help batching, so during peak you get more batching efficiency but cache may have lower hit rate if queries are more diverse. conversely, steady traffic from product tours yields higher hit rates. we should run TTL sensitivity to see how quickly hits decay.
03:10 - Maya: action: Priya can flip cache TTL to 1h on staging and run 48h, that will tell us decays and real savings.
03:18 - Priya: yep will do.
03:20 - Jonah: another lever is model variant r-7b-quant vs r-3b-int4. the 3b int4 showed 30% lower token cost per inference in our microbenchmarks but a higher error rate on some QA tasks. so there's a quality vs unit cost tradeoff.
03:37 - Ari: that aligns, we need to maintain answer quality for core flows. maybe use 3b for low-risk auto-summarization and 7b for customer-facing completions.
03:46 - Marco: routing policy then? send low-risk calls to cheaper variant. how hard is that to set in Redwood?
03:52 - Jonah: we can set route by tag at the API layer or have the app decide. Redwood supports auto-fallback on capacity pressure too, so we can route to 3b when 7b pool is saturated.
04:05 - Maya: okay let's talk dollars Maya pull up the spreadsheet (not shown in transcript). our estimate earlier: with current traffic mix (2.4M active monthly prompts) hosted cost is projected at about $12k/month with baseline config. switching to dedicated reserved capacity reduced unit cost by ~22% in our simulation, at an incremental committed spend.
04:30 - Priya: what's the commitment threshold where dedicated becomes cheaper?
04:33 - Maya: roughly at sustained 1.5M generated tokens/day or about 45M tokens/month on our profile. If you're below that, hosted might still be simpler.
04:45 - Ari: do you include caching and batching effects in that dedicated calc?
04:49 - Maya: yes, the model assumed a conservative cache hit of 20% and batching similar to our measured windows. we'll refine after Jonah's 24h run.
04:58 - Marco: and what about pre-warm overheads and cold start? our flows have occasional big synchronous requests where cold-start latency matters.
05:06 - Jonah: cold start on dedicated is negligible; hosted has a bit more variance. we measured cold path p95 ~1.2s on hosted during low traffic. with dedicated pool and pre-warmed replicas it's under 400ms.
05:20 - Ari: sounds like dedicated may be worth it for reliability even if cost parity is marginal.
05:24 - Maya: agreed, but the sales/commercial side will model commitment vs flexibility. we'll share both scenarios.
05:30 - Jonah: one more thing batching strategy: we tested batching windows by time-slicing vs size-slicing. time-slice 20ms cap gave more predictable latency but slightly lower throughput. size-slice to 64 maximized throughput but p95 variability. dynamic hybrid gives best of both in many workloads.
05:52 - Priya: any quick wins to lower unit cost without affecting p95?
05:56 - Jonah: yes tighten prompt templates to reduce average generated tokens by ~5-8%, enable client-side prefilter to drop non-actionable queries, and increase cache TTL where applicable. Also quantization to int4 on low-risk models helps a lot.
06:15 - Marco: about 5-8% from prompts is interesting that's product-level work. we'll try a prompt redesign A/B.
06:21 - Ari: can Redwood run a comparative cost report for us showing hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid for our actual traffic?
06:26 - Maya: yes I'll produce a cost model with tokens/sec/$ columns and scenarios at 1M, 3M, and 6M monthly prompts.
06:34 - Jonah: for the 24h run I'll include per-window breakdown: tokens generated, cache hits, avg latency, p95, tokens/sec, and tokens/sec per USD.
06:42 - Priya: also export full traces so our infra team can replay specific tails.
06:46 - Jonah: yup will include logs and model traces; redacted where necessary.
06:50 - Maya: competitor question Ari asked about Anthropic and OpenAI costs, where do they compare?
06:56 - Ari: we just want a sanity check, not necessarily switch.
06:58 - Jonah: quick take OpenAI endpoints can be cheaper for certain workloads but less flexible for private deployments; Anthropic pricing similar but varies by model. Redwood's differentiation is predictable dedicated unit economics and caching/batching levers which give extra savings at scale.
07:15 - Marco: ok sounds good.
07:18 - Maya: recap Jonah runs 24h benchmark, Priya enables TTL=1h on staging, Ari to confirm cost SLO and p95 target, Maya sends pricing spreadsheet.
07:28 - Ari: confirm p95 target we can accept up to 600ms p95 for customer flows, but internal tooling can go to 1s.
07:35 - Maya: got it, will note that in next Steps.
07:38 - Priya: quick question on security for on-prem pilot we need KMS integration and audit logs. is that standard?
07:44 - Jonah: yes we support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and detailed audit logs in Private deployments. we'll surface the compliance docs as part of the pilot pack.
07:56 - Maya: perfect. any other blockers?
07:58 - Marco: none from product.
08:00 - Ari: no. thanks all.
08:03 - Maya: we'll follow up with notes and send scheduling for the pilot kickoff. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words and filler present; speaker labels approximate.
